THE DH-SUFFIXED TWIN OF THE ACCEPTED 'PurposeCode' ROW ABOVE, missed only because this list keys on exact fieldId. Added 2026-09-04 after it blocked EVERY provider: CHECK 5 is read by enforce on all 20, so this single field turned the whole portfolio BLOCKED and report_mission_status to 0 of 20. FormInput in 12 providers (a 1-char code prefilled 'C'), FormSelect in CA_eSUN (a value-list dropdown, attributeTypeId=DEX_INQUIRY_PURPOSE_CODE). CA_eSUN IS THE CORRECT ONE AND IT WAS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED: its engineering-built v1.0 -- the configuration running live at San Diego Sheriff -- carries 5 FormSelect purpose controls, which is precisely why DEX-1313 exists to convert that DROPDOWN to radio buttons. Building it as FormInput would delete the officer-selectable purpose code SDSO actually uses. Same adjudication as the PurposeCode row: provider metadata decides, and both are valid.

SCOPED TO SC_SLED ONLY -- everywhere else a FormInput raceCode is still a FAIL. This is NOT a 'both are valid' row like the ones above: it is a capability we GAVE UP, on purpose, and the row exists so the reason survives. SC_SLED v1.3 moved WantedPersonQuery to its OWN TAB at Rob's request ('now move wanted person to its own tab' / 'start with option A  we can work backwards if we have to'), which is possible because tabs are keyed by QUERYINPUTFORM not by entity (CAPABILITY #47). But LIMITATION #28 breaks codeTypeProvider reverse-lookup for any entity carrying two QIFs, and AP #1 says the consequence is the platform transmitting its INTERNAL NUMERIC ROW ID instead of the code -- silently wrong Race data to SLED, which is worse than a clumsier control. So raceCode is a FormInput here with the valid values in its label ('type W, B, I, A or U'), and its codeTypeProvider is removed from the wpAttrs attribute only. TO WORK BACKWARDS: move the card back onto Person and restore Sel + codeTypeProvider; that is the v1.2 shape.

SCOPED TO SC_SLED ONLY -- a FormInput SexCode on any of the other 20 providers is still a FAIL, which matters because this is the single most widely-built control in the portfolio. Same cause as the raceCode row: the WantedPerson tab puts SexCode on a two-QIF entity, LIMITATION #28 kills its reverse-lookup, and AP #1 makes the untranslated value an internal numeric id on the wire. Label carries the values ('type M, F or U'). NOTE that SC_SLED ALSO builds SexCode as a FormSelect WITH codeTypeProvider on its Person tab (Driver License card) and that one is UNAFFECTED -- Person still has exactly ONE QIF -- so this provider legitimately contains both shapes and the divergence is intra-provider as well as cross-provider.

SCOPED TO SC_SLED ONLY -- a FormInput RegistrationState anywhere else is still a FAIL, and that matters because all 21 providers build this control. THIRD ROW OF THE SAME ADJUDICATION as raceCode and SexCode above, and the third capability GIVEN UP to place a tab. SC_SLED v1.8 moved AdministrativeMessage from targetEntity='Article' to 'Boat' because Rob asked for it LAST in the strip ('put admin at the end like i asked') and the tab-order rule MEASURED off the v1.7 tenant says a tab can only be last if it sits on the LAST entity: the order array's duplicate entity entries carry no information, forms of one entity render in configurations[] order, so SAME-ENTITY TABS ARE ALWAYS ADJACENT. That makes Boat a TWO-QIF entity, LIMITATION #28 breaks its codeTypeProvider reverse-lookup, and Boat's State was exactly the rescue pattern it depends on -- Sel with attributeTypeId='STATE' (which ALONE sends the platform's internal numeric row id, AP #1) paired with codeTypeProvider='NCIC' on the BoatQuery attribute to resolve it back to a 2-char code. Keeping the dropdown would have put a numeric id on the wire where SC expects a state code. So the Boat control is a FormInput with the format in its label ('State (2-char code; leave blank for SC)') and the attribute's codeTypeProvider is removed. COST MEASURED BEFORE CHOOSING, not rationalised after: State is any[]-ONLY on both Boat combos (QBBQ.H, QBBQ.R), so it is a pure optional and NOT a routing discriminator -- no BUILD_RULES 24 exposure. WHY BOAT BORE IT AND NOT ARTICLE: Article hosts a second QIF for FREE because ArticleTypeCode resolves on the CONTROL (codeTypeCategory NCIC_ARTICLE_TYPE / codeTypeSource CA_CLETS) and NO Article attribute carries codeTypeProvider or attributeTypeId -- so #28 has nothing to break there. Article is simply not the last entity. NOTE SC_SLED ALSO builds RegistrationState as a FormSelect on Vehicle and Person, both single-QIF entities, and those are UNAFFECTED -- so like SexCode this divergence is intra-provider as well as cross-provider. TO WORK BACKWARDS: move AdministrativeMessage back to a non-last single-QIF host and restore Sel + codeTypeProvider; Administrative Message then renders adjacent to that host instead of last.
